questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The location, the weather, the culture, the prestige of the school and the proximity to the ocean

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say that it was pretty hard especially considering covid and long wait times at the embassy and noone really knowing procedures, threre were a lot of I dont knows from everyone I asked and with some aspects not a lot of information to go from.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received none started by living in a hotel until I could move into my off campus housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They did the best they could given the covid situation I guess with that being said there wasnt really done much in terms of explaning how things work.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is pretty hard, but if one has an open mind and a not too smal budget it of course makes things esaier

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I can definetely recomend if you are going here to experience america in generel it makes sense, with that being said if one is going for the college experience or social life staying on campus makes more sense especially in the international housing which seem to be the most social housing on UCSD

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just do it their website its very straightforward, I will remark though that for a lot of courses you have to "lucky" to get it so sit ready when your first pass opens dont pospone it. also sometimes and sometimes not you can be helped to skip the waitlist try to ask I got yes in my first quarter for 2 courses I got a lot of nos my second quarter.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation I think but else you get email with instructions if you are ever in doubt contact student services or international counseling or what ever they are called very helpfull :D

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didnt get one of the classes I really wanted sadly.

questions.answer: You just do it their website its very straightforward, I will remark though that for a lot of courses you have to "lucky" to get it so sit ready when your first pass opens dont pospone it. also sometimes and sometimes not you can be helped to skip the waitlist try to ask I got yes in my first quarter for 2 courses I got a lot of nos my second quarter.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Its very different from University of Copenhagen expect to have a lot of exams and "busy" work and not just a final at the end of your couse

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses are in generel a good bit esaier than back home, I have heard that this should be espcially true for humanaties and social sciences.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I do belive it was much much better, I have much more of a sense of the professor actually caring if I learn something, TA are in generel more helpfull but maybe also less knowledgeable and the class structures are often very well structured and very straigthforward. In generel you can expect everything to just work here and make sense, and if something doesnt it is very likely you can dm the professor and get a thoughout answer.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
MATH	183 statistical methods David Quarfoot or something like I believe to be the best teacher I have ever had.
CSE	150B 	AI: Search and Reasoning Sean Gao is very knowledge come to his office hours and ask interst questions if you want and he will be glad to answer also the course structure is very practical no bullshit and straightforward.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Public Transport sucks here, I would definetly recomend trying to buy a car especially if you know what you are doing, everyone here will have a car btw. even people living on campus. So that was a big unexpected cost in generel everything is a tad more expensive than copenhagen expect living the same standard of life to cost about 1,5x.

Also when ever you are drinking you will of course have to use uber or lyft as you and your friends cant drive and again public transit sucks.
Downtown san diego is relatively far away from la jolla where UCSD is which also means transportation cost goes even higher.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food is more expensive than I expected I expected it to be a good bit cheaper it is about the same to a tad more expensive.
Gas became expensive because of the ukraine crisis.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went to the gym several times, I know they organize trips that I can recomend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definetly go roadtripping california is amazing along the coast, also I went to coachella also a huge recomendation there, I went to yucatan mexico visiting merida and cancun was also an amazing experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Definetly go roadtripping california is amazing along the coast, also I went to coachella also a huge recomendation there, I went to yucatan mexico visiting merida and cancun was also an amazing experience. 

You will be surprised what you can manage in a weekend also if you maybe include friday I went to las vegas for a friday saturday sunday for example.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: People are very friendly dont be afraid to just talk to people sitting next to you its way more normal here and people will think you are cool just for not being american.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Honestly no challenge with the american in generel, maybe that one should get acustomed to that just because americans say something doesnt really mean you have a deal they can pull back on the day of the event and thats quite normal.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How outgoing people were and the whole gotta go get it kinda mindset.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The schol is located a good bit from Downtown san diego and public transport is non existen biking is also pretty hard as the road are not made for it and very mountainy/hilly, there is really nothing besides the school and you spend a lot of time transporting yourselves again I would recomend to consider buying a car.
UCSD is known for being UC socially dead while it is possible to find partys it definetly has that nickname for a reason, in international housing you will find the people who like to party, with the above being said people are still outgoing and friendly. 

Another thing is that be prepared to see that about 50% of people are asian, which means that culture also is a huge part of the generel vibe.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont think so try to have as litle stuff going on back home as possible when you leave so you can really emerge your self

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going to coachella and roadtriping up and down the coast was amazing.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Haha common theme but the transportation, and honestly the comunication with university of copenhagen about pre-approval amongst other things.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
